title: metadata.json — the database's texts and images, projected
description: Sits at the root of the item folder, next to item.json; the images it lists sit in metadata/ beside it. It is not a document anyone edits: it is what the catalog database held about this item at the moment asOf names, written by the one service that owns the item and replaced whole on every projection. There is no merge, so there is no conflict, and no revision to keep in step. A rebuild restores these texts and images exactly as the last projection left them. Per-user state — progress, lists, settings — is never here.

allOf.$comment: An ordering is a decision about a series; a place in one is a property of an episode.

itemId.description: Equals the itemId of item.json in the same folder.

asOf.description: The state of the database this file is a projection of. A later projection replaces the whole file.

primary.description: Display title. May differ from the title item.json recorded at creation.

credits.description: People, by reference. The person's own texts and images are not copied here: personId keys the person the database holds.

personId.description: Stable: person pages are user-facing URLs keyed by it.

series.description: Present only on a series: the series as a whole and every season the database knows, whether or not its episodes are on storage. Which episodes ARE on storage is the episodes/ folders themselves; nothing lists them, so adding an episode never rewrites this file.

tmdbSeason.description: Kept here too, so a season with no episodes on storage keeps its reference id.

name.description: Anthology and anime seasons carry their own titles.

episodeCountReference.description: Episodes the reference database lists, to show gaps against the episode folders.

episode.description: Present only on an episode. The episode's own name and overview are in titles; its numbering is in item.json.

images.description: Every image file in metadata/. Each is named by the hash of its own content, so an image is written once and never replaced in place: a new image is a new file, and the projection that stops naming an old one lets it be collected. A missing kind falls back to the parent at read time (an episode without a still shows its season poster, then the series poster); nothing is copied.

file.description: metadata/<content hash>.<ext>: the lower-case hex sha256 of the file's own bytes, and the extension matching contentType. No subfolders.

season.description: On a series: the season this image belongs to; null for the series itself.

language.description: For posters and logos with text, the language of that text. The file name carries no language, so this is the only record of it.

sha256.description: The same digest the file name carries, in the form the rest of the format uses. Caches key on it.

sourceUrl.description: Where the image came from, so the exact chosen image can be fetched again.

videos.description: Trailers, teasers and clips published elsewhere, by reference. A downloaded, packaged trailer is listed in the version's package.json instead.

key.description: The site's id for the video.

library.description: The decisions the database holds about this item's storage. Nothing here is a fact about the bytes — those are in the version, source and package records, which are written once and measured. These are choices a person or the catalog made that no measurement could recover, so they are projected with the texts and a rebuild restores them.

primaryVersionId.description: The version that plays when the viewer does not choose. Null when the database never decided, and a reader then picks for itself. It is a decision, not a place: it never moves a file.

versionLabels.description: versionId -> what a viewer picks between, e.g. 'Director's Cut', 'Black & White'. Listed only where a person set one; every other version is labelled at read time from its edition and presentation, so an unlisted version is not an omission.

match.description: Whether and how this item is identified against the reference database. item.json carries the reference ids; this says how far to trust them, so a re-sync can skip what is unmatched or disputed and never overwrite what a person decided.

reference.description: Facts as published. Deliberately separate from the version's MEASURED runtime: a reference database lists one runtime for every cut.

defaultOrdering.description: Series only: the ordering a viewer sees unless they choose another. The orderings themselves are not listed here — each episode records its own place in each of them, so adding an episode never rewrites the series.

numbering.description: Episode only: where this episode sits under each ordering it appears in, which is the whole record of that ordering — nothing on the series repeats it. Its aired entry agrees with the seasonNumber and episodeNumber item.json was created with, and no two episodes of a series may share a place in one ordering.

episodeEnd.description: Set when this one file covers several episodes.

curation.description: What a person decided about the texts and images, projected with them so a rebuild does not hand a locked item back to automation.

fieldOrigins.description: Where each value came from, keyed by field path. Lists only fields that are set. Images carry their own origin.
